justification: The repository exhibits severe lack of decomposability: main.py (1,000+ lines) bundles command definitions, data persistence, configuration loading, state management, and business logic into a single monolithic module. Static analysis confirms 'avg_fan_out': 13.33 and 'factors': ['C1', 'C2', 'A3'] indicating high coupling and poor modularity. The 3-file structure (config.py, app.py, main.py) with 0 packages shows no module boundaries. This violates decomposition principles: commands are hardcoded in HELP_CATEGORIES dicts, handlers are scattered inline, and state variables are global. Decomposability directly addresses this by isolating concerns into separate modules (e.g., commands/, persistence/, utils/), reducing cognitive load and limiting change scope.
expected_architectural_change: main.py will be split into multiple focused modules: commands/ (command handlers), persistence/ (data loading/saving), utils/ (helpers), models/ (data structures), and a minimal main.py orchestrator. config.py will be refactored into a dedicated config/ module with typed settings. This creates clear module boundaries and reduces fan-out.
implementation_strategy: 1. Extract command handlers into commands/admin.py, commands/media.py, etc., each with dedicated handlers and minimal imports. 2. Move data persistence logic (load_data/save_data) into persistence/storage.py. 3. Create models/state.py for global state encapsulation. 4. Refactor config.py into config/settings.py with validation. 5. Update main.py to import and register modules. 6. Introduce a command dispatcher pattern to reduce direct if/elif chains.
risks: Risk of temporary duplication during migration; requires careful import graph management to avoid circular dependencies. Mitigation: migrate one category at a time, use integration tests to verify behavior, and maintain backward compatibility during transition.
